description: The one classification of every .gaia/local entry, transcribed by hand from the frozen state-model classification (never generated from code, which is what is under correction). Consumers read this instead of hand-maintaining their own lists. `path` is relative to .gaia/local/. A `path` may join more than one concrete on-disk shape with '|' when a single logical entry covers several filenames (e.g. a clearance marker's .ok/.refused siblings); each '|'-joined alternative is matched independently under the entry's own `match` rule. A `path` may also carry a '<placeholder>' token for a variable path segment (a spec id, a digest, a worktree name); for `match: glob` a placeholder behaves as a shell '*' wildcard, and for `match: prefix` only the literal text before the first '<' is significant. `residue` lists known dead-feature/legacy paths that are real on some machines but are not live state: reported if found, never treated as drift and never a live entry.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per-clone value; correct via idempotent overwrite, no partition key needed
entries.why: Per-clone /gaia-init and /setup-gaia step-completion record. A per-tree copy would re-run setup steps per worktree, which is wrong for a fact about the clone, not the tree.

entries.keyed_by: session id, one file per Claude Code session
entries.why: The statusline writes each session's context reading (<session_id>.json, tmp + mv) for the audit loop's checkpoint to read. Anchored to the main root so every worktree's render lands in one place the bound hook finds. Must precede cache-shared, whose prefix would otherwise claim these files first.
entries.reaped_by: check-updates.sh (sweeps regular files older than 7 days on its TTL-gated pass)

entries.keyed_by: singleton machine-scoped caches, each overwritten in place; update-gaia/<tag>/ additionally partitions by release tag
entries.why: Machine-scoped release/update-check and statusline-guard state (update-check.json, update-gaia/<tag>/, serena-guard/) that is a property of the machine, not of any one tree. Per-session context readings under context/ are the separate context-readings row, which precedes this one.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per machine
entries.why: Machine-local, lower-only override of the audit checkpoint's context line. Lives in the protected folder and is hand-authored by a human; Claude tool writes to it are denied by block-audit-loop-write.sh.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per machine
entries.why: GAIA's per-machine opt-ins (the statusline left-side choice). Written by /setup-gaia and read by the statusline from every tree; not write-guarded, unlike protected/checkpoint-override.json.
entries.source: statusline left-side choice, added after the frozen classification

entries.keyed_by: content digest over the files the audited member owns (per member)
entries.why: A clearance marker attests a Code Audit Team member reviewed content; in git the tree is the content, so the key is the content, and the symlinked drop zone lets one gate judge every checkout's markers.

entries.keyed_by: base-sha plus branch, computed by gaia_audit_key (.gaia/scripts/audit-key-lib.sh); base-sha alone collides across worktrees cut from one main tip
entries.why: Co-written into the symlinked audit store; the branch discriminator is the missing partition that keeps two trees' findings from overwriting each other.

entries.keyed_by: base-sha plus branch, computed by gaia_audit_key (.gaia/scripts/audit-key-lib.sh), plus the member -- the same partition the findings sidecar uses, and for the same reason (base-sha alone collides across worktrees cut from one main tip)
entries.why: The scope-time digest a Code Audit Team member attests to, written where the member resolves its review scope (.gaia/scripts/audit-scope-digest.sh --capture) and read back where it writes its clearance (--read), so the marker cannot attest content that moved under the review.

entries.keyed_by: HEAD sha
entries.why: Redacted local security detail, keyed by the commit it describes, in the shared audit store.

entries.keyed_by: singleton store; a cross-tree file lock plus self-identifying rows (session_id + spec/plan id + seq)
entries.why: An append-only cost ledger every tree contributes to; correctness comes from the lock, not from partitioning.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename, last rename wins
entries.why: The machine-local rate table pricing reads. It holds adopter-authored prices (an edited row is never replaced by a sync), so it is not regenerable cache and must not be treated as one.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename, last rename wins
entries.why: The per-model merge base: the distributed rows as of the last sync plus feed-written rows. The sync compares the local table against it to tell an edited row from an untouched one.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename, last rename wins
entries.why: A byte copy of the main checkout's distributed rate table at the last sync; a difference from the current distributed file is what triggers the next sync.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename, last rename wins
entries.why: The rate feed's backoff and not-found record, stored as epoch integers so a failed or empty fetch is not retried within the hour.

entries.keyed_by: one copy per recovery, named by epoch seconds plus a mktemp suffix
entries.why: Unreadable local rate tables preserved before the table is reseeded, so a hand-edited price is never silently destroyed.
entries.reaped_by: token-rates-local-lib.sh on each new preservation (keeps the 5 newest)

entries.keyed_by: one mktemp name per write, never reused
entries.why: In-flight temp files of the rate table writes and the feed response body, present between creation and the rename. A process killed mid-write can leave one behind; it is inert (nothing reads it) and has no reaper.

entries.keyed_by: singleton store; the shared cost mutex plus self-identifying rows (session_id + key + first_ts; cursor rows by session_id + role + path)
entries.why: Append-only usage ledger of segment, binding, and cursor rows. Every tree contributes, so correctness comes from the lock and the self-identifying rows, not from partitioning; attribution is resolved at read time.

entries.keyed_by: singleton store; the shared cost mutex plus self-identifying rows (edge and unlink rows by child + parent + ts; merge rows by pr + key)
entries.why: Append-only lineage ledger of edge, unlink, and merge rows. Written by any tree under the same mutex as the usage ledger; readers apply tombstones at read time.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename under the mutex
entries.why: Regenerable cache folded from the usage ledger's cursor rows: the latest offset per transcript file. Deleting it re-reads from the ledger, never loses a row.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; temp-file-then-rename, lock-free, last writer wins
entries.why: Regenerable cache of branch-name derivations and per-store read offsets for the usage readouts. Deleting it, or any corruption, only makes the next readout derive from scratch; it holds no attribution.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per clone; atomic mkdir
entries.why: Singleton guard for the SessionStart transcript sweep, so two sessions starting together do not both parse the backlog.

entries.keyed_by: one mktemp name per write, never reused
entries.why: In-flight temp files of the usage writers, present between creation and the rename or append. A process killed mid-write can leave one behind; it is inert (nothing reads it). Only the branch memo's temps have a reaper; every other writer's temps have none.
entries.reaped_by: usage.sh readouts reap .usage-branch-memo.tmp.* older than 60 s; other writers' temps have none

entries.keyed_by: singleton; idempotent overwrite of a cache whose authority is a repo-global GitHub fact
entries.why: A worktree debt fix must arm main's count cache, not a discarded per-tree copy; the authority is the GitHub tech-debt label, not this file.

entries.keyed_by: the tree key (gaia_tree_key, .gaia/scripts/main-root-lib.sh): the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over this working tree's physically-resolved root. The entry addresses itself at red-ledger/<tree_key>/, so it stays private to its tree once .gaia/local is shared.
entries.why: A RED observation is a claim about one working tree at one commit; sharing it across trees would be a category error. The identity rule's own reference example of correctly per-tree state.

entries.keyed_by: the tree key (gaia_tree_key, .gaia/scripts/main-root-lib.sh): the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over this working tree's physically-resolved root. The entry addresses itself at worthiness-ledger/<tree_key>/, so it stays private to its tree once .gaia/local is shared.
entries.why: A worthiness observation is a claim about one working tree's emergent-surface tests at one commit, the same kind of per-tree fact as a RED observation. It lives under worthiness-ledger/, outside the wholesale-symlinked audit/ segment, so it is per-tree by the same mechanism as its RED-ledger sibling: gaia_registry_linkable_paths only symlinks scope:"shared" entries, and this one is not.

entries.keyed_by: the tree key (gaia_tree_key, .gaia/scripts/main-root-lib.sh): the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over this working tree's physically-resolved root. The entry addresses itself at forensics/<tree_key>/, so it stays private to its tree once .gaia/local is shared.
entries.why: A human-facing local forensics report read in the checkout that produced it; no cross-tree consumer. Named in the write-guard's own non-exempt list.

entries.keyed_by: the tree key (gaia_tree_key, .gaia/scripts/main-root-lib.sh): the first 16 hex characters of a sha256 over this working tree's physically-resolved root. The entry addresses itself at handoff/<tree_key>/, so it stays private to its tree once .gaia/local is shared.
entries.why: The one live handoff for this tree's session; a handoff written in one tree and read from another is exactly the wrong-tree confusion the checkout-boundary guard exists to catch.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per-clone ledger keyed internally by finding_class; atomic replace without a cross-tree lock, so simultaneous writes can drop one decline and re-offer that candidate
entries.why: The operator's declines on the machine's hardening candidates. The candidate set is the repo's merged-PR window and the nudge it feeds is machine-scoped, so one copy per clone is the only scope at which a decline can suppress what it declined. Shared through the registry-driven symlink, so a decline recorded in a linked worktree lands in the main checkout's copy and survives that worktree's removal.

entries.keyed_by: singleton per-clone snapshot; atomic replace, so a review completed in one tree unconditionally supersedes another's
entries.why: What a completed /gaia-harden review saw: the audited-PR denominator, the class inventory, and when it ran, plus the start-of-run tally it was built from. The nudge it silences is machine-scoped like the decline ledger, so one copy per clone is the only scope at which a review can discharge what it reviewed. Shared through the registry-driven symlink, so a review completed in a linked worktree lands in the main checkout's copy and survives that worktree's removal.
The SPEC-number allocation's authority is the remote immutable spec/NNN tag; the ledger is main's cache and the plan reference contracts the SPEC-NNN folders to the main checkout.
The plan folder stays in the main checkout by contract; worktree-mode orchestrators write PROGRESS.md back to main.

GAIA's documented research location. A research Write under the main checkout's research directory binds the session's default-branch spend at read time, so the directory must resolve to main's copy from every tree.

A PR-capture written under main's cache for the merge flow, main-anchored not per-tree, and partitioned per-branch in the filename (cache/gh-artifact-pr.<branch-slug>.json) so two worktrees opening PRs concurrently no longer share one unkeyed last-writer-wins file. Still main-only rather than shared: worktrees reach this file by resolving main's root, they are never given their own linked copy, so keyed_by stays null per the schema's rule and the key shows up in `path` instead.

The residue triage command's derived read cache (per-pull-request attribution and resolved cited lines, keyed by pull-request number and head sha) and its resumable per-run cursor. Derived state, never a record: a cold cache reproduces the same candidate list. Main-only rather than shared, so keyed_by stays null per the schema's rule and the two concrete filenames show up in `path` instead. Named `residual`, not `residue`: this registry's own top-level `residue` array names an unrelated concept, orphaned machine-local state with no automatic reaper.

Per-branch audit loop history and allowance, resolved to main so every session, sub-agent, fork and linked worktree on the branch reads one record. Lives in the protected folder; written only by the audit loop hooks.

One identity per clone, used in ping/telemetry. Forks per worktree path today via a hash of the repo root path, a defect; classified at its main-only target scope with the fix deferred to a later phase.
An update-preference file written only from main in the shipped workflow, because the /update-deps flow refuses to run from a linked worktree before any write happens.
Read-anchored to main (the statusline command resolves to main) or operator-authored per machine; single copies with no per-tree meaning. Hand-authored, not GAIA-generated.
Per-machine markers (a sandbox-resolution result, a short-lived setup sentinel); one value per clone.

This program's own pre-allowlisted artifact for a future update-driven migration; no shipped writer exists yet. Its eventual scope is a forward inference (main-anchored, matching every other update-flow cache, since /update-gaia and /update-deps both refuse to run from a worktree) rather than a fact about shipped code.
The live in-flight SPEC draft, its pre-dispatch retry snapshots, and the gate-1 drift-detection snapshot for one authoring session; keyed by spec id, deleted at canonical save or on discard.
Per-tree session shape (start time, Socratic question-ceiling counter) for one SPEC-authoring session; the holder's own working state, keyed by spec id, stays where it is written.
The session-host liveness lock for one SPEC-authoring session; deliberately resolved to main so the cross-tree mutex is reachable from both trees, keyed by spec id.
Self-review and adversarial-audit scratch (per-lens findings, refutation verdicts, coverage log) for one in-progress SPEC-authoring session; keyed by spec id, deleted at canonical save or discard.

One Code Audit Team member's private working copy for the one kind of evidence that needs real bytes on disk: breaking a construct a guard names to establish the guard is not hollow. Each member names its child with its own member name, which keeps two co-dispatched members from overwriting each other's tree, and removes it when done.
entries.source: gaia-react/gaia#1447, added after the frozen classification

entries.why: A cost-ledger breadcrumb recording whether an adversarial audit ran this SPEC or plan session; deliberately resolved to main, keyed by spec/plan id, read-then-deleted by the cost tally.
A defer-flag cache for SPEC/plan wiki promotion, and a per-UAT content-hash mirror for the UAT-write idempotency check; both keyed by SPEC or plan id.
gaia-react-perf measurement run output, keyed by run id.
/gaia-audit findings reports and transient gh-issue-body staging files, keyed by timestamp/run stamp, self-pruned by their own producer in the shared audit directory.

Maintainer health-audit per-run bucket-executor output and its Comprehensive-phase sibling, keyed by run stamp, self-pruned to a bounded number of recent runs by the health-audit runbook, in the shared audit directory.

entries.keyed_by: the normalized branch key with its branch: prefix dropped (slashes nest), or session-<session id> for a detached HEAD; one folder per key, never shared between keys
entries.why: Execution-doctrine run folder (STATE.md checkpoint, findings, log.md) written by Claude through Bash while a branch or worktree session runs. Shared so a worktree's folder lands in the one main-anchored store and a resumed session finds it from any tree. Small; a reaper is a filed follow-up, so reaped_by is null for now.

entries.keyed_by: tree root, one line per linked worktree; read-modify-write under a cross-tree mkdir lock, written temp-then-mv
entries.why: The main-anchored slot ledger: which linked worktree holds which port slot. One ledger for every tree is the point, so two worktrees can never be handed the same ports.
entries.reaped_by: slot reclaim in worktree provisioning and in the ports session-start cleanup

entries.keyed_by: one file per retired ledger entry, named <slot>.<epoch>.tsv
entries.why: A reclaimed slot's leftover servers must still be found and stopped after the ledger line is gone. One file per entry means a reaper deletes it with rm and never rewrites a shared file.
entries.reaped_by: the tombstone reap once no listener on the slot's ports qualifies for a removed-tree stop, or after 7 days

entries.why: A singleton mkdir lock serializing ledger rewrites across trees, with no partition key. Held only for the read-modify-write, never across a signal or a wait.
entries.reaped_by: broken once when older than 60 seconds

entries.keyed_by: server PID, one file per server a Claude session launched
entries.why: Records which dev or Storybook server a Claude session started, with its process identity, so a dead session's server can be stopped after the identity is re-verified. A human's launch is never recorded.
entries.reaped_by: the dead-session reap (ports session-start cleanup and worktree provisioning); the tombstone reap prunes the records of a reclaimed tree

entries.keyed_by: Claude Code session id, one file per session
entries.why: Records each live session's host process so a launch can be attributed to it and a dead host can be told from a live one.
entries.reaped_by: the dead-session reap, when the host is dead and no launch record names the session

entries.why: Per-session dedupe marker written by workflow-doctrine-inject.sh (tmp + mv, through Bash) holding the last injected key so startup, resume and tool events do not re-inject an unchanged doctrine. Anchored to the main root, never the entered tree. One tiny file per session; a reaper is a filed follow-up, so reaped_by is null for now.

residue.why: Opt-in config for the removed mentorship feature; a stray one has no reaper.
Removed mentorship feature's cloud event stream.
Orphaned marker from the removed mentorship feature; both its writer and reader are gone.
Residue pattern from a deleted carry-forward feature; no current writer anywhere in the codebase, and no reaper if one is ever found.
Residue pattern from a deleted out-of-scope disposition sidecar; no current writer anywhere in the codebase, and no reaper if one is ever found.
Per-checkout sentinel from a removed feature's one-time cleanup pass; transitional residue with no live writer.
Legacy pre-existing archived-plan layout; the live plan-archive path reduces a plan folder in place today and does not move it here. Read only by repair and migration tooling.
Legacy pre-existing archived-SPEC layout; the live spec-archive path reduces a SPEC folder in place today and does not move it here. Read only by repair and migration tooling.

rm_whitelist.why: Archived plan folders are regenerable scratch an agent may clear; the plans/ ledger itself is main-anchored state that is never bulk-deleted, so only its children are whitelisted.
Individual spec-scratch folders are clearable, but specs/ is the main-anchored SPEC store and is never bulk-deleted; children only.
Audit markers and reports are self-pruning scratch; the shared audit/ store is symlinked structure that is never bulk-deleted; children only.
A per-tree handoff file is disposable session scratch; the handoff/ container is kept, only its contents are cleared.
Cache entries are regenerable machine/session scratch; the cache/ container is kept, only its contents are cleared.
Per-branch run folders and their dispatch artifacts are scratch the PR Merge Workflow pre-clears by absolute path before each dispatch; the runs/ container is kept, only its contents are cleared.
Build output regenerated by the build; safe to remove wholesale (rm -rf dist), so the directory itself and its children are both whitelisted. Repo-root-relative, outside .gaia/local.
Build output regenerated by the build; safe to remove wholesale, directory and children alike. Repo-root-relative, outside .gaia/local.

integrity_snapshot.why: Durable, leaf-authored SPEC folders; a destructive script deleting one must be caught, never mistaken for background churn.
Durable, leaf-authored plan folders and their PROGRESS ledgers; irreplaceable working state a run must not silently alter.
The live per-tree session handoff; leaf-authored durable content, unlike the background-churned debt/telemetry/audit/cache/red-ledger dirs the snapshot deliberately excludes.
